saints.name: St. Clement I
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: One of the first successors of St. Peter, whose letter to Corinth is among the oldest Christian writings after the New Testament…
biography: Clement was one of the earliest bishops of Rome, counted third in succession after St. Peter, and reigned near the close of the first century. His letter to the Church of Corinth, written to heal a division there, is one of the most precious documents of the sub-apostolic age and an early witness to the authority of the Roman Church.

According to tradition he was exiled and put to death under the Emperor Trajan, cast into the sea bound to an anchor, which became his emblem. His name too is remembered in the Roman Canon, and his supposed relics were later brought to Rome and enshrined in the basilica of San Clemente.
saints.knownFor: His early letter to the Corinthians and his witness as an apostolic pope.
